ticket.summary: Update field definition for Date Partition in Monthly Datasets
ticket.description:
The field definition for date partition is accurate for datasets that are not monthly since it reflects the date the data was ingested. For monthly datasets, it is actually the end date of the month. We will need to update these definitions in the metadata so that it can flow through to Snowflake and to ThoughtSpot. 

Update for Snowflake and in DataSetMetaData if it exists for the monthly datasets.

New definition:   
The closing date of the month for which the data has been aggregated

ticket.summary: Use Spark for heavy RA copy jobs
ticket.description:
Convert the heavy RA copy jobs (datasets that are generally large like Relationship FS, Loan FS Breakdown, Core Loan Accounts, etc.) to using the new Spark copy runner in <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://qtwo.atlassian.net/browse/DE-2357</custom>.

‌

That was done for just Rel FS and just for Truist DV (it was also a bit rushed to get them over the line). It would be good for this ticket to further test that runner that it syncs properly with DatasetMetadata, copies data over the same as it did with the pandas runner. 

‌

See how little resources we need (1 executor with minimal memory?) to be able to handle large files. For reference, Rel FS for 7d8 in alpha is \~3.7gb and for Truist DV was \~27gb. Truist DV was able to handle that find with the default spark configs, (3 executors with 16gb memory. Most likely overkill).

‌

I don’t think we need to do this for the really small RA files, so we dont have to spin up so many concurrent Spark executors.

‌

It may be worth either using Claude to go through and find clients + copy jobs that meet a certain threshold (for example taking more than 10 minutes?) 

‌

General Steps:

1. Validate the primary Relationships FS for Truist DV (c3563e8a-3e29-45e9-9dad-9e6743126d78) data. See if the CSV output from DatePartition=20260226 (pre Spark) is of the same format as anything after DatePartition=20260312. You can just see if the same primary keys exist and if they have the same data, or if some fields have the same values or date fields are produced the same
2. Look for RA copy job candidates to convert to spark
3. Configure for those clients

merged_pull_requests.name: DE-2368: Moving To Spark Ingestion Runner
merged_pull_requests.description: # Checklist for Author and Reviewers - [x] considered batch vs Spark job - [x] new functionality is unit tested - [x] dataset version incremented, if appropriate - [x] dependencies on this job? -> engineering dataset - [x] paths constructed [using ActivityContextPath](https://confluence.q2ebanking.com/display/DI/Handling+Paths+in+Task+Code) - [x] integration testing validated - [x] job is "rundate aware", if appropriate - [x] update Databricks and/or Snowflake, if appropriate - [x] Was this tested in Alpha Airflow - [x] If version was incremented were copy jobs incremented as well in DAG code? (Please attach screen shots of copy job logs) - [x] was data populating as expected and not just null For additional details, see [Job Checklists and Processes](https://confluence.q2ebanking.com/display/DI/Job+Checklists+and+Processes) # Follow-on Checklist - [x] job has been scheduled - [x] contx metadata has been updated - [x] alpha integration tests successful - [x] [dataset metadata changelog](./ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/data/README.md) has been updated # Description Ticket: [DE-2368](https://qtwo.atlassian.net/browse/DE-2368) This ticket involved: 1) finding which job-client combinations merited moving to Spark. If a client exceeded 10 minutes for an ingestion job -- i.e., a job formatted as `get_` -- the client likely had 2+gb to move. This roughly makes it worthwhile to move to Spark as a heuristic. You may find all of the job-client combinations in this file within the archived OpenSpec `md` -- `openspec/changes/archive/2026-04-10-add-ra-ingestion-overrides-for-slow-multi-client-jobs/normalized-target-clients.md`. One more criteria: the job had to be compatible with the `SparkRaCsvIngestionRunner`. For that reason, `get_client_uploaded_files, get_core_loan_amortization_tables` did not qualify due their existing structure. 2) Finding Desired Spark Config Currently Spark has the following config: In testing, adding more compute or executers did not substantially lower execution time. Rather, the extra memory sat idle. This is because the Spark Ra Runner depends in `I/O` of the data lake. The read capacity is the main bottlekneck in our system. 3) Per-Job `SparkRaCsvIngestionRunner` Find in `ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/primary_ingestion/ra`. I based new runners off of @plmnguyen work in `relationship_financial_statements.py`. 4) Applying Configuration Within `dags/precisionlender/dags/task_groups/main/ra_jobs.py`, I made a class for `DynamicRaIngestion`. These `get_` jobs are dynamic in that they can be `spark` or `batch`. Then `get_dynamic_ra_ingestion` takes in job and client to provide desired configs. If not spark client, their configurations do not change. If they are Spark, we apply the new runner and configuration as listed above. # Testing Take the override client `32743a57-2030-4fa5-aadd-756ade802493 ` and for a non-override client does not have spark jobs: All jobs complete for `32743a57-2030-4fa5-aadd-756ade802493`. Integration testing: Consider the Spark Job for `32743a57-2030-4fa5-aadd-756ade802493`. We must validate that the code in master yields that same out as that resulting from DE-2368. I will show that the before-after CSV do not differ for one of the Spark Jobs with `core_commercial_loan_account` as the example. Generated by Spark: Generated with Pandas: Indeed they are the same before and after spark! Also ran sanity check in Staging. For the client `5301628b-e85f-4ff9-b5b3-e8d13c5926a7`, there are two Spark Jobs, which is what we see in the following picture and corresponding [link](https://airflow.staging.precisionlender.com/dags/l3-main-5301628b-e85f-4ff9-b5b3-e8d13c5926a7/grid?search=l3-main-5301628b-e85f-4ff9-b5b3-e8d13c5926a7&dag_run_id=manual__2026-04-01T05%3A00%3A00%2B00%3A00&tab=graph&task_id=ra_group.get_core_loan_amortization_tables)

ticket.summary: LoanAmount doubled for opportunities with conversion loans - using wrong source field
ticket.description:
Opportunities with conversion loans show doubled LoanAmount values (e.g., $4.8MM instead of $2.4MM). **We are currently using the wrong field.** We extract and sum commercialLoanAccounts\[\].amount, but we should be using

  allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount instead.

‌

  **Current** **(Wrong)** **Field:**

  commercialLoanAccounts\[\].amount - extracted from each individual loan account and summed together. This includes both the original loan and its conversion loan, causing duplication.

‌

  **Correct** **Field:**

  allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount - pre-aggregated at the scenario level by PrecisionLender. This field already contains the correct total and does not double-count conversion loans.

‌

  **Files** **to** **Change:**

‌

1. ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/data/opportunities/pipeline_scenarios_opportunities_history_v1.py

* Add allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount to SCENARIO_COLS

* Remove amount extraction from COMM_LOAN_COLS and MC_COLS

2. ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/data/opportunities/opportunities_helpers.py

* Remove LoanAmount/LoanAmountMC aggregation logic from aggregate_account_array_columns()

* This function currently sums the array of individual loan amounts. Since allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount is already a single pre-aggregated value (not an array), the aggregation logic is no longer needed and would fail if left in

  place.

‌

  **Acceptance Criteria:**

* \[ \] LoanAmount uses allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount instead of summed individual accounts

* \[ \] Opportunities with conversion loans show correct (non-doubled) amounts

* \[ \] Unit tests updated
